### Whether the pipeline ran, not what it produced

Every panel reads Prometheus, fed by Airflow's StatsD through statsd-exporter. **There is deliberately no datasource for the serving database** — that data is read in Metabase, and two dashboards over the same tables drift until only one is trusted (stack §8).

The DAG and task ids are *labels* here rather than parts of the metric name, which is what `pipeline/monitoring/statsd_mapping.yml` buys. Without it every DAG is its own series name and nothing below can be grouped.

*Panels use Grafana's default datasource rather than naming one. A dashboard in git cannot reference a uid Grafana generates per volume, and pinning one broke provisioning outright: "Datasource provisioning error: data source not found".*

⚠️ **Airflow 3.3 emits less to StatsD than its docs suggest.** `dagrun.duration.*` and `dag_processing.import_errors` never arrive — checked at the exporter, not assumed — so no panel here queries them. What does arrive is task duration, task successes/failures, and per-operator counts, all labelled by the mapping file.

panels.title: Task failures by operator
panels.description: Separates "the Docker containers are failing" from "a Python task is failing" without opening a log. Replaces an import-errors panel: Airflow 3.3 does not emit dag_processing.import_errors to statsd, so that panel could only ever be blank.

panels.title: Task outcomes
panels.description: Successes and failures across every DAG. A flat line at zero on both means nothing ran at all, which looks healthier than it is.

panels.title: Time spent per DAG
panels.description: Summed task duration per DAG -- the closest real answer to "how long does a run take". Airflow 3.3 does not emit dagrun.duration.* to statsd, so a dagrun-duration panel would read empty forever.

panels.title: Slowest tasks in the pipeline
panels.description: Which step is the cost. snowflake_stage and load_serving dominate; a change in the shape here is usually a change in volume, not in code.
